comparison.event_time_check: Each newly written twin event has UTC offset zero and a timestamp within the corresponding call window plus or minus one second.
comparison.write_effects: Every paired write adds one event per case. Returned write data agrees with each case's own ledger; status and projected event streams agree across cases.
comparison.read_effects: For status, gate, next_task and trace, CLI and MCP outputs agree exactly on each case and ledger bytes do not change. Twin case states agree after narrow project-field normalization.
comparison.run_replay: The same manifest applies one item on each case; CLI and MCP summaries agree. A second run skips that item and leaves both ledger byte streams unchanged.
comparison.signed_approvals: The same signed synthetic case accepts one valid Ed25519 signature through MCP and a second valid signature through installed CLI --signature. Status reports both as signed_verified; removal of trust invalidates both. This is not a same-challenge twin-case equality assertion.

limits: The assertions cover these operation paths and states, not all possible inputs, errors or states.
Audit timestamps and hashes differ naturally between twin cases; UTC timing is checked per call, not exact timestamp equality.
The signed approvals use a synthetic in-memory key and do not represent consent, identity or authority of a real human.
The SIGKILL follows a published checkpoint and the paired CLI writer barrier does not prove a ledger-read collision or model-agent concurrency.
The wheel is a local build artifact and is not committed. No field intervention or controlled model comparison is shown.
